source_text:
Διὰ φιλοξενίαν καὶ εὐσέβειαν Λὼτ ἐσώθη ἐκ Σοδόμων, τῆς περιχώρου πάσης κριθείσης διὰ πυρὸς καὶ θείου, πρόδηλον ποιήσας ὁ δεσπότης, ὅτι τοὺς ἐλπίζοντας ἐπ’ αὐτὸν οὐκ ἐγκαταλείπει, τοὺς δὲ ἑτεροκλινεῖς ὑπάρχοντας εἰς κόλασιν καὶ αἰκισμὸν τίθησιν.
συνεξελθούσης γὰρ αὐτῷ τῆς γυναικὸς ἑτερογνώμονος ὑπαρχούσης καὶ οὐκ ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ, εἰς τοῦτο σημεῖον ἐτέθη, ὥστε γενέσθαι αὐτὴν στήλην ἁλὸς ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης, εἰς τὸ γνωστὸν εἶναι πᾶσιν, ὅτι οἱ δίψυχοι καὶ οἱ διστάζοντες περὶ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ δυνάμεως εἰς κρίμα καὶ εἰς σημείωσιν πάσαις ταῖς γενεαῖς γίνονται.
thought_title: Lot saved, his wife made a sign
orientation: Clement is giving examples from Scripture of how faith, hospitality, and obedience bring salvation while envy and double-mindedness bring judgment, now turning to Lot and his wife.
pass_a_gloss: Through hospitality and piety Lot was saved from Sodom, [with] the whole surrounding region having been judged through fire and brimstone, [the] Master having made [it] clear, that those hoping upon him he does not abandon, but those being double-inclined he places into punishment and torment. For [with] his wife having gone out together with him, being of a different mind and not in harmony, into this sign she was placed, so as [for] her to become a pillar of salt until this day, for [it] to be known to all, that the double-souled and those doubting about the power of God become for judgment and for a warning to all generations.

choices.why: The word means leaning to the other side, wavering between two directions; 'double-inclined' preserves the compound sense and matches the parallel δίψυχοι (double-souled) later in the passage.
The term literally means two-souled, describing a divided inner self; the literal rendering keeps the psychological force and the parallel with 'double-inclined'.

choices.english: for judgment and for a sign
choices.why: The double prepositional phrase is emphatic; keeping both 'for' phrases preserves the parallel structure and the sense that such people become both a verdict against themselves and a warning to others.
rejected: as a judgment and a warning
for condemnation and as an example

choices.why: δεσπότης denotes absolute ownership and authority; 'Master' is the standard rendering and distinguishes this title from κύριος (Lord).

choices.term: ἑτερογνώμονος ὑπαρχούσης καὶ οὐκ ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ
choices.english: being of a different mind and not in harmony
choices.why: The phrase describes a disposition contrary to her husband's; 'of a different mind' keeps the literal sense of ἑτερογνώμων, and 'not in harmony' uses the glossary term for ὁμόνοια.
rejected: being of a contrary opinion and not in agreement
having a different judgment and not in unity

bible_refs.note: ἐτέθη, ὥστε γενέσθαι αὐτὴν στήλην ἁλός (she was made a pillar of salt)

pass_b_english: Because of his hospitality and piety, Lot was saved from Sodom when the whole surrounding region was judged with fire and brimstone. The Lord made it clear that he does not abandon those who hope in him, but hands over to punishment and torment those who lean another way.

For when his wife went out with him, she was of a different mind and not in harmony. She was made a sign of this: she became a pillar of salt and remains so to this day. This was so that everyone would know that the double-minded and those who doubt the power of God become a judgment and a warning to all generations.

problems.quote: become a judgment and a sign
problems.source_quote: εἰς κρίμα καὶ εἰς σημείωσιν πάσαις ταῖς γενεαῖς γίνονται
problems.why: γίνονται with double εἰς means 'become/are made into' i.e. 'serve as'; but 'become a judgment' obscures that they themselves become the judgment/sign. More importantly, σημείωσιν means 'warning, admonition' (the act of signifying), not 'sign' (σημεῖον). The double-souled become a warning/admonition, not a sign.
problems.fix: become a judgment and a warning to all generations
problems.ruling: σημείωσιν is 'warning/admonition' (act of signifying), not 'sign' (σημεῖον). Reader misled by conflating two distinct words.

edits.old: become a judgment and a sign to all generations
edits.new: become a judgment and a warning to all generations

fixed: Changed 'sign' to 'warning' in the English and the literal gloss, since σημείωσιν means 'warning, admonition' rather than 'sign' (σημεῖον).

problems.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
problems.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.

problems.why: Literal translation of Greek 'dipsychoi'; 'double-minded' is standard.

fixed: Changed 'Master' to 'Lord' for consistency with the divine title used elsewhere in the translation.
Changed 'double-souled' to 'double-minded' as the standard English rendering of the Greek term.

polish.changed: Split the long passage into two paragraphs at the turn from Lot's deliverance to his wife's fate, and clarified the sentence order so the sign and its purpose follow naturally.

last_rejected.quote: become a judgment and a warning
last_rejected.source_quote: εἰς κρίμα καὶ εἰς σημείωσιν πάσαις ταῖς γενεαῖς γίνονται
last_rejected.why: γίνονται with εἰς = 'become for/as', but 'warning' for σημείωσιν is weak; σημείωσιν means 'sign, mark, token', not warning. 'Sign' or 'example' better.
last_rejected.fix: become a judgment and a sign to all generations
last_rejected.ruling: σημείωσιν denotes a sign/mark; 'warning' is within normal range as a sign serving warning purpose, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: she was made a sign of this
last_rejected.why: English 'she was made a sign of this' loses 'τοῦτο' (this/that); the sign specifically refers to her lack of harmony, not just the salt pillar itself.
last_rejected.fix: she was made a sign of this very thing
last_rejected.ruling: 'of this' translates τοῦτο; no omission. Claim misreads English, which correctly includes τοῦτο as 'this'.
